thread:
Alice Nguyen: Proposal — I want to reorganize our Terraform modules: split GPU pools, VPC, IAM, and KMS into focused platform modules under modules/platform/* and keep thin compatibility wrappers so existing workspace configs don't break. Need a safe canary + state-migration strategy. Thoughts?

Ben Howard: Do you mean moving resources into new modules and changing references, or creating new workspaces? main worry is state moves and drift. :eyes:

Alice Nguyen: Both. Plan A: introduce new modules but keep wrapper modules named the same as today that forward to new implementations. Then perform an explicit state migration for a single canary workspace using `terraform state mv` and validate plan. Plan B (fallback) is create new-workspace + tf import for the canary and switch routing.

Carol Park: Compatibility shim sounds good — a wrapper like `module "gpu_pool" { source = "modules/platform/gpu" }` that keeps the same outputs/inputs. Consumers see no change. That buys us time to migrate states.

Alice Nguyen: Exactly. Example shim:```hcl
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "../../modules/platform/gpu"
  name   = var.name
  size   = var.size
}

output "pool_id" {
  value = module.gpu_pool.id
}
```

Ben Howard: For the actual state move we'll run a dedicated migration workspace to avoid breaking CI. Example commands for the canary:```bash
# targeted state move for canary workspace
terraform state mv 'module.old_gpu.google_compute_instance.instance[0]' 'module.new_gpu.google_compute_instance.instance[0]'
terraform plan -out=plan.canary
terraform show -json plan.canary | jq .
```

DevOps Bot: trigger:terraform-canary: started apply for workspace=infra-gpu-reorg-canary by=alice Nguyen

Henry Li: KMS/IAM part needs care. If we change key resources, avoid re-encrypting S3/GCS by creating new key and then rotate alias instead of destroying old key. Also ensure service accounts keep required roles during migration: add temporary role bindings in the shim module.

Alice Nguyen: Good call. Plan: create new KMS key in the same project, grant decrypt/encrypt to existing service accounts, then switch alias. We will not destroy old key until after a 30d cooldown.

Maria Gomez: Cost note — splitting GPU pools could fragment capacity and raise bin-packing inefficiency. Suggest we use a shard sizing policy and a reservation/generation tag so autoscaler can merge workloads across shards when underutilized. Also quantify: expect ~3–6% potential price delta in worst fragmentation.

Carol Park: We can add a helm/values flag for shard tuning for the autoscaler:```yaml
gpuPool:
  shardSize: 16
  mergeThresholdPct: 25
```

SRE Oncall: We need a runbook and a 2-hour maintenance window for the canary apply. Steps: backup state, run plan, run apply in canary, smoke tests (routing, inference latency, KV cache sanity), rollback plan. Put alerts to slack on failure.

Ben Howard: Who owns the migration run? I can do the migration workspace run and the state moves if Carol provides the shim PR. Will need someone to watch the cluster metrics during canary (latency/cold-starts/gpu-util).

Alice Nguyen: Action items: 1) Carol to open shim PR + unit tests for outputs (by EOD) 2) Ben to own migration apply for canary (schedule tomorrow 09:00 PST) 3) Henry to prepare KMS alias + policy 4) Maria to model cost impact and shard recommendations 5) SRE Oncall to prepare runbook and postmortem template.

DevOps Bot: ci:pr:12345 checks passed (terraform fmt, validate, tflint)

Carol Park: PR created: https://git.company/repo/pulls/12345 — contains wrappers and a migration checklist. :rocket:

Ben Howard: I'll start a dry-run this afternoon in a sandbox workspace and post plans here. If plan looks clean we'll do canary tomorrow. :thumbsup:

SRE Oncall: Scheduling 2h window tomorrow 09:00–11:00 PST. Noted — will add monitoring dashboards and runbook link to the calendar invite.

Alice Nguyen: One more note: add gating on gitops (Argo/Flux) so the new module changes only get applied to canary workspace first. We should also add a pre-apply hook that fails if any non-metadata resource diff touches more than X resources.

Ben Howard: Agree. I'll add a pre-apply script that checks `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` and ensures changed_count < 10 for canary.

Maria Gomez: For cost forecasting I'll simulate split with current usage traces and share a short report before the canary.

Alice Nguyen: OK — sounds good. Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after Ben's dry-run. :white_check_mark:
